summary: Lease and token timing, as settled on 10/25: the lease every minute, 5-minute tokens, a new host token only near its end, clients renewing from the answer.

provisional.why: Above 60 and below 120 seconds. The backend team sets the exact value.
The field name is not fixed by the backend team yet.

planPosition: The spread sizes, and that the spread only ever moves a call earlier.

lease.rule: The takeover time is always above the renewal interval, so a live Crew never loses its lease.

mintThreshold.rule: A renewal that finds less than the threshold left on the current host token gets a new one. The threshold sits a little above a minute because lease calls carry a random spread, and at exactly 60 seconds a call landing a few seconds early would find more than a minute left and the next would come too late.

hostToken.alsoIssued: On the first call, and when hostTokenRequested is set.

spread.why: So Crews and clients that reconnected together don't renew in the same second.

clock: Time the next call from when the answer arrived, with a monotonic clock, using renewInSeconds. If it is missing, use the token's own lifetime, exp minus iat, less 60 seconds. Never compare exp with the device's clock.

outage.effect: A Kiro backend outage longer than about a minute drops remote connections, each when its token runs out. Within 5 minutes every one has ended. They come back as soon as minting does. Accepted on 10/25.
outage.recovery: When the backend recovers, every Crew and client that missed a renewal renews at once: at most one signature for each connected Crew and each open client, about 275,000 to 580,000 at the capacity target. The random spread and the jittered retry backoff flatten it.

exampleSequence.gets: host token 2, exp 2026-11-02T17:08:45Z, sent to the relay in a token frame
